answer: A market for relic catalogs and garden terrace surveys can make seller guarantees resistant to disposable aliases. Escrow each seller's earned revenue until its job liability expires, and cap all outstanding guarantees at that escrow balance. A new identity starts with no guarantee capacity; splitting escrow among keys preserves the total insured exposure. An attacker must lock additional capital to sell additional guarantees, and proven non-delivery consumes the backing. This limits exit fraud without claiming that account keys identify distinct operators.
